threads.body:
theres some differencs in the partition handling between 2.8 and 2.9

see https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/pull/19566

`stripPartitionSuffix` can throw `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` when `TopicName.getPartitionIndex(topicName)` returns a non-`-1` value for a topic that does *not* contain `TopicName.PARTITIONED_TOPIC_SUFFIX` (e.g., `my-topic-1`). In that case `suffixIndex` is `-1`, and the substring call at lines 56–58 becomes invalid. Add an explicit `if (suffixIndex == -1) { return topicName; }` before the substring logic.

replies.body:
Addressed in e54a765571a93f7be834c868a003662c31fe8593.

Analysis: Pulsar 2.8 can infer a partition from any numeric topic tail, so parser output alone cannot identify a canonical partition suffix. A shared suffix-index helper now verifies that `-partition-` exists and that its exact text matches the parsed index; production destination naming, partition IDs, and integration-test expectations all use those criteria, with a regression test for a numeric tail without the suffix.

Upsides: Prevents the stable-semconv substring exception, avoids emitting a partition ID for an unchanged non-partitioned destination, and keeps test expectations aligned with production behavior.

Downsides: The integration-test expectation intentionally duplicates the production validation algorithm, so future changes to the criteria must update both.

threads.body: `destinationPartitionId` currently trusts `TopicName.getPartitionIndex` even in cases where `stripPartitionSuffix` intentionally refuses to treat the topic as partitioned (e.g., `...-partition-key-7` or `...-partition-01`). This can emit `messaging.destination.partition.id` for a destination name that still includes the full topic, creating inconsistent/incorrect semconv output. Make `destinationPartitionId` apply the same “valid suffix” check as `stripPartitionSuffix` (suffix present and equals the parsed index) and return `null` otherwise (or refactor into a single helper that returns a validated partition index used by both methods).
